item.text: {"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"For 2023, the supplied record does not establish that Félix Tshisekedi enacted, funded, staffed, inspected, enforced, or corrected a nuclear command-and-control or physical-custody system. The DRC was subject to relevant safeguards and physical-protection obligations through its IAEA agreements and Pelindaba membership, but these state-level commitments do not demonstrate presidential implementation, resourcing, inspection performance, accident prevention, or remediation during the period. Tshisekedi did issue and attribute security-force directives, including a mixed army-police patrol for the Francophonie Games, a directive to unify and support the FARDC, and a stated plan to create and supervise an Armed Defence Reserve for Wazalendo fighters; the supplied sources do not establish implementation, effective controls, or safety outcomes. Broader force-governance evidence is adverse or mixed: the government supported Wazalendo and FDLR forces, contracted private military personnel, acquired armed drones, and used operational orders during the August 2023 Goma operation that treated protesters as enemy auxiliaries and authorized force under broad exceptions. These facts concern conventional and irregular force control rather than nuclear custody and do not prove personal responsibility for every operation, but they provide no basis for treating the broader safety-governance record as demonstrably effective. The answer is therefore negative as to demonstrated effective nuclear safeguards, with substantial attribution and evidence gaps rather than a finding of proven nuclear-control failure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0017-E004","BATCH-0023-E019","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0019-E010","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0011-E019","BATCH-0028-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0019-E003","BATCH-0011-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No supplied evidence documents nuclear command-and-control, physical custody, nuclear inspections, safety funding or staffing, accident records, enforcement, or correction of identified nuclear-safety failures in 2023.","IAEA and Pelindaba records establish ongoing state obligations and safeguards context, not Tshisekedi-attributed implementation or effectiveness during the target period.","The Francophonie patrol, FARDC directive, Armed Defence Reserve, Wazalendo/FDLR support, private military personnel, armed drones, and Goma orders concern broader conventional or irregular force governance; they are only qualified analogues and cannot substitute for nuclear-control evidence.","Official directives and the campaign account of the Armed Defence Reserve do not establish implementation, resourcing, supervision quality, or outcomes.","The Goma operational orders are attributed to subordinate commanders and higher-level authorization is not shown to have been personally approved by Tshisekedi; the broader government attribution also does not establish control over every aligned group.","The adverse methane-auction reporting concerns a hazardous non-nuclear domain, is not needed to establish this answer, and does not prove personal presidential direction or benefit."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization that Tshisekedi's directives and institutional reforms demonstrated meaningful command-safety governance.","Reframed treaty and safeguards evidence as state-level context rather than evidence of presidential implementation or effectiveness.","Added the supplied evidence on the Armed Defence Reserve, Wazalendo supervision claims, private military personnel, armed drones, and operational force-control concerns, with explicit non-nuclear and attribution qualifications.","Reduced the methane-auction material to a limitation rather than substantive support.","Preserved favorable directives and institutional actions as qualifying evidence without inferring implementation or safety outcomes."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review would be warranted if additional 2023 evidence identifies DRC nuclear facilities, radioactive-material custody arrangements, IAEA inspection findings, national nuclear-safety institutions, budgets, trained personnel, incident reporting, or corrective actions attributable to Tshisekedi.","The broader force-governance concerns may require separate verification of presidential authorization, operational control, and documented safety or civilian-protection outcomes before being used more strongly in this lens."]}
